api:
<Alluvial data={passengers} value={|p: &Passenger| p.count}>
    <Stage name="Class" value={|p: &Passenger| p.class} />
    <Stage name="Sex" value={|p: &Passenger| p.sex} />
    <Stage name="Survived" value={|p: &Passenger| p.survived} />
</Alluvial>
PropTypeDefault
dataas above: one row per item or group of itemsrequired
children<Stage name value>: one column each; value is Fn(&T) -> &strrequired
valueFn(&T) -> f64: how many items the row stands for1. per row
node_width, node_padding, link_opacity, tooltip, classas on <Sankey>

Built on the same layout and painter as <Sankey>. Each stage is a column of categories with its name on top. Bands keep the colour of the first stage's category all the way across, so you can follow a group through every stage. The same category name gets the same colour in every column.

examples.title: Titanic passengers
examples.description: Each band follows one group of passengers through four stages, coloured by class.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn passengers() {
    let data = use_signal(titanic());
    rsx! {
        <Alluvial data={data} value={|p: &Passenger| p.count} class="h-96">
            <Stage name="Class" value={|p: &Passenger| p.class} />
            <Stage name="Sex" value={|p: &Passenger| p.sex} />
            <Stage name="Age" value={|p: &Passenger| p.age} />
            <Stage name="Survived" value={|p: &Passenger| p.survived} />
        </Alluvial>
    }
}
